title: General Knowledge
subtitle: A bit of everything worth knowing

cards.prompt: How many continents are there in the most common count?
cards.note: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America. Some countries count the Americas as one continent and arrive at six.

cards.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
cards.note: It covers about a third of the Earth's surface, more than all the land put together.

cards.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
cards.note: It hangs in the Louvre in Paris behind bulletproof glass. A theft in 1911 is what really made it world famous.

cards.prompt: Which is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level?
cards.note: It stands about 8,849 metres tall. Measured from the Earth's centre, Chimborazo in Ecuador wins, because the Earth bulges at the equator.

cards.prompt: Which river is traditionally considered the longest in the world?
cards.note: At about 6,650 km the Nile usually comes first, though some measurements put the Amazon slightly ahead. The Amazon clearly carries the most water.

cards.prompt: How many bones does an adult human have?
cards.note: Babies are born with around 300 bone elements. Many of them fuse during childhood, for example in the skull.

cards.prompt: Who wrote the German drama "Faust"?
cards.note: Goethe worked on it for about 60 years. Faust Part Two was only published in 1832, shortly after his death.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
cards.note: Au comes from the Latin aurum. The similar-looking Ag is silver, from argentum.

cards.prompt: How many players of a football team are on the pitch at once?
cards.note: Ten outfield players plus the goalkeeper. If sendings-off leave a team with fewer than seven, the match is abandoned.

cards.prompt: How many keys does a standard piano have?
cards.note: 52 white and 36 black keys, spread over a little more than seven octaves.

cards.prompt: What is the largest animal on Earth?
cards.note: It grows up to about 30 metres long and over 150 tonnes. That makes it bigger than any known dinosaur.

cards.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers?
cards.note: Roughly 900 million people speak Mandarin as their first language. Count second-language speakers too and English comes first.

cards.prompt: How many seconds are there in a day?
cards.note: 24 × 60 × 60 gives 86,400. The number shows up constantly in programming, for example when converting timestamps into days.

cards.prompt: How many squares does a chessboard have?
cards.note: 8 × 8 squares. The legend of the grain of rice that doubles on every square shows how fast exponential growth explodes.

cards.prompt: Who composed the "Moonlight Sonata"?
cards.note: Piano Sonata No. 14 only got its nickname after Beethoven's death, from the poet Ludwig Rellstab.

cards.prompt: Which country has the largest population?
cards.note: According to UN estimates, India overtook China in 2023. Both countries have a little over 1.4 billion people.

cards.prompt: Which is the largest country on Earth by area?
cards.note: Russia spans eleven time zones and is about 1.7 times the size of Canada in second place.

cards.prompt: In which city does the famous leaning tower stand?
cards.note: It started to lean during construction in the 12th century because the ground is too soft. Extensive repairs around the year 2000 reduced the tilt.

cards.prompt: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
cards.note: Standard tuning from low to high is E A D G B E. Mnemonic: "Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie."

cards.prompt: What is the currency of Japan?
cards.note: The character 円 means "round". The Korean won and the Chinese yuan go back to the same character.

cards.prompt: Who developed the theory of relativity?
cards.note: His 1921 Nobel Prize was not for relativity, though, but for explaining the photoelectric effect.

cards.prompt: How many colours does a rainbow have in the classic division?
cards.note: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. The number seven goes back to Isaac Newton; in reality the spectrum is continuous.

cards.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
cards.note: In adults it covers about 1.5 to 2 square metres. The largest internal organ is the liver.

cards.prompt: How many federal states does Germany have?
cards.note: Three of them are city states: Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen.

cards.prompt: On which continent is the Sahara?
cards.note: It is the largest hot desert on Earth. Strictly speaking, Antarctica is the largest desert, because it gets almost no precipitation.

cards.prompt: Who wrote "Romeo and Juliet"?
cards.note: The play is set in Verona. Shakespeare did not invent the story; he adapted it from older Italian novellas.

cards.prompt: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
cards.note: Its chemical symbol is Hg. Gallium melts at just under 30 °C, so in your hand, but at room temperature it is still solid.

cards.prompt: How many days does a leap year have?
cards.note: Rule of thumb: years divisible by 4 are leap years, but full centuries only if divisible by 400. That is why 2000 was a leap year and 1900 was not.

cards.prompt: In which country is the Inca city of Machu Picchu?
cards.note: It was built high in the Andes in the 15th century. The Spanish conquerors never found it, which is why it is so well preserved.

cards.prompt: What is Edvard Munch's most famous picture called?
cards.note: Munch made several versions as paintings, pastels and lithographs. You can see them in Oslo, at the National Museum and the Munch Museum.
